# [S1, unofficial] Snaps user-drawn path to detected feature boundaries using edge detection and Dijkstra shortest path.

The claim states that the tool snaps user-drawn paths to detected feature boundaries using edge detection and Dijkstra shortest path. The evidence explicitly supports this in the notes ('A boundary confidence image is blended with the slices to provide uncertainty information... user selects the region using a guided uncertainty-aware lasso that automatically snaps to detected feature boundaries') and in the contributions section ('A guided uncertainty-aware lasso for region selection, based on edge detection and Dijkstra shortest path algorithms'). The passage also confirms the lasso 'automatically snaps to the detected feature boundaries'.
supported

*   **When to Use:** When exploring complex, multivariate volumetric data (e.g., seismic, medical) where manual TF tuning is tedious and user domain knowledge can guide feature selection [S1, unofficial].

The evidence explicitly states that the proposed method (GuideME) is designed for 'highly complex datasets' such as 'multimodal MR brain scans' (medical) and 'real-world seismic dataset' (seismic). It further confirms that the method replaces 'tedious trial-and-error transfer function tunings' with an automated workflow. Additionally, the text notes that the user 'detects a feature of interest using his/her domain knowledge,' which aligns with the claim that user domain knowledge guides feature selection.
